appraisal_events.evidence: "Swann, avec son ostentation, avec sa manière de crier sur les toits ses moindres relations, était un vulgaire esbroufeur que le Marquis de Norpois eût sans doute trouvé...puant"; the narrator elaborates at length how the once exquisitely discreet Swann now boasts loudly of Mme Swann's humble new acquaintances.
appraisal_events.explanation: The father's blunt verdict is corroborated and expanded by the narrator's own account of Swann's new vanity, marking a clear fall from his earlier reputation for social delicacy, even though the narrator explains it sympathetically as a natural displacement of habitual virtues.

appraisal_events.evidence: "devenu, à la longue, notoriété européenne"; "les plus intelligents des jeunes médecins déclarèrent...que si jamais ils tombaient malades, Cottard était le seul maître auquel ils confieraient leur peau."
appraisal_events.explanation: Despite an earlier reputation for awkward timidity, Cottard is now recognized even by the most discerning younger doctors as a clinician of unmatched sureness, an unambiguous rise in his professional standing.

appraisal_events.evidence: Radical cabinets ideologically opposed to him repeatedly entrust him with extraordinary missions; the Journal des Débats itself calls such men statesmen; governments prize the prestige of his aristocratic name and trust his political loyalty absolutely.
appraisal_events.explanation: Norpois is portrayed as an exceptionally valued and trusted figure whose aristocratic prestige and reliability make him sought after even by governments that should distrust him.

appraisal_events.evidence: "M. de Norpois passait pour très froid à la Commission...où chacun félicitait celui-ci de l'amitié que lui témoignait l'ancien ambassadeur"; "tout le monde en est stupéfait à la Commission où il n'a de relations privées avec personne."
appraisal_events.explanation: Colleagues openly remark on and congratulate the father for a warmth from the notoriously cold Norpois that no one else receives, publicly marking a rise in his local standing even though the father himself is puzzled by it.

status_effects.explanation: Swann's old exquisite discretion is replaced by vulgar, self-serving boasting about his wife's humble new connections, a clear local fall in estimation.
The medical profession's own most discerning younger members openly declare Cottard the doctor they would trust with their lives, a clearly witnessed rise in his professional reputation.

Successive governments, even ones ideologically opposed to him, repeatedly entrust Norpois with high missions and prize his aristocratic name, a clearly witnessed and endorsed elevation of his standing.
Colleagues at the Commission publicly note and envy a friendship with Norpois that no one else enjoys, marking a modest but clearly witnessed rise in the father's local standing.
